tldr: An Oct 17 paper (EPGM) proposed tracking execution provenance so agent memory retrieval stays within a budget. On Oct 23 LangChain described the retrieval techniques its Deep Agents harness uses against clumsy searches, oversized results and stale data.
whats_new: Oct 29: "Retrieval as Traversal" proposes value-indexed memory so long-context agents stop re-searching for what matters on every forward pass.
why_it_matters: Agent memory is shifting from bigger stores to cheaper retrieval: provenance, result sizing and indexing decide context cost and staleness.

status.detail: Two arXiv papers and one LangChain engineering post in 12 days; only LangChain's describes a shipped harness.

beats.headline: EPGM adds execution provenance to budgeted agent memory retrieval
LangChain: context engineering for agents starts with retrieval
Value-indexed memory recasts retrieval as traversal

open_questions: Do EPGM or the value-indexed memory paper release code or numbers on production agent workloads?
Does LangChain publish measurements of its retrieval techniques in Deep Agents?
take_for_builders: Audit your agent's retrieval for oversized results and stale data, and log which memory entries each answer used; treat the papers as research until code appears.
